issues.t: Water on the driver's floor from a clogged A/C drain
issues.sym: The carpet on the driver's side (sometimes the passenger side) gets soaked, there is a musty smell, and in bad cases water drips onto the pedals.
issues.why: Condensation from the A/C is supposed to drain out through the firewall. On the Endeavor the drain area clogs with debris and broken-down insulation, or a foam seal fails, so the water backs up into the cabin. Mitsubishi issued several service bulletins with fixes such as a secondary drain or a longer drain tube.
issues.next: Have the A/C drain cleared and ask the shop to apply the Mitsubishi bulletin fix so it doesn't come back. Dry the carpet and padding fully to stop mold, and check for damp wiring under the carpet.

issues.t: Fuel filler pipe rusts and leaks (recall)
issues.sym: A strong gas smell or fuel dripping near the right rear wheel, often while you are filling the tank. A check engine light can also appear.
issues.why: Mud and road salt get trapped against the filler pipe and its bracket and rust through the pipe. Mitsubishi recalled 2004-2010 Endeavors in salt-belt and cold-weather states and extended the pipe warranty elsewhere.
issues.next: Don't ignore a fuel smell. Ask a Mitsubishi dealer to check your VIN for recall 10V065000; if it is done or doesn't apply, have the pipe inspected and replaced if it leaks.

issues.t: Automatic transmission flares or shifts harshly
issues.sym: The engine revs briefly between 2nd and 3rd gear, shifts feel harsh or late, or the vehicle shudders or vibrates when shifting into 4th.
issues.why: RepairPal lists a 2-3 shift flare as the most common Endeavor problem and links it to an internal transmission fault. Worn fluid and clutch packs make it worse with age.
issues.next: Check the transmission fluid level and condition and have codes read. A fluid service and software or valve body repair may help early; slipping that keeps getting worse usually means a rebuild.

issues.t: Check engine light from vacuum leaks
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on. The engine may idle a little rough or unevenly.
issues.why: Cracked or loose vacuum hoses and intake seals let unmeasured air into the engine, which the computer flags. RepairPal lists this as a common Endeavor problem.
issues.next: Have the codes read and a smoke test done to find the leak. It is usually a hose or gasket.

issues.t: Rear subframe rusts and suspension arm breaks loose
issues.sym: Clunking from the rear, a wheel that leans or tucks in, the SUV pulling or wandering, or visible heavy rust under the rear.
issues.why: In salt-belt states the rear subframe and control arm mounts corrode. Owners report the upper A-arm mounting tabs and rear control arms breaking, which can let a rear wheel collapse.
issues.next: If you live where roads are salted, have the rear subframe and arm mounts inspected every year. Stop driving and tow the vehicle if a rear wheel looks out of line.

issues.t: Key comes out when shifter isn't in Park (recall)
issues.sym: You can pull the key out even though the shifter is not fully in Park, and the parked SUV can roll away.
issues.why: The ignition key interlock cable can let its cam fall forward, so the lock that holds the key until Park is selected does not work.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake. Ask a dealer to check for recall 08V139000, which inspects and fixes the interlock for free.

issues.t: Fuel tank strap bracket can split (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing you can notice. In a severe crash the tank could drop and leak fuel.
issues.why: The left rear fuel tank strap bracket may have been stamped incorrectly and can split near a bolt.
issues.next: Have a Mitsubishi dealer check for recall 08V454000. They inspect the bracket and reinforce it if it is split.

issues.t: Defroster airflow switches on its own (recall)
issues.sym: Air suddenly moves from the windshield to other vents, or the temperature swings between hot and cold, which can fog the windshield.
issues.why: On models with manual A/C, a faulty control signal can damage the mode door shaft and send air to the wrong vents.
issues.next: If the windshield fogs, pull over safely. Ask a dealer for recall 10V514000, which inspects and repairs the mode door shaft for free.

issues.t: Passenger seat belt anchor can break (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing you can see in normal use. In a severe crash the front passenger belt may not hold.
issues.why: The lower anchor bracket for the right front seat belt can separate in a hard crash.
issues.next: Ask a dealer for recall 08V022000. They replace the passenger seat belt and bracket for free.

issues.t: Seat side airbag bracket badly welded (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing you can see. In a side crash the seat-mounted airbag may not deploy correctly.
issues.why: On Endeavors built from late May to late July 2009, a bracket that holds the seat side airbag may not have been welded properly.
issues.next: Ask a dealer for recall 09V361000. They inspect the weld and replace the seatback if needed.

issues.t: Parking brake cable nut can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: The parking brake feels weak or doesn't hold the SUV on a slope.
issues.why: The lock nut on the parking brake pedal cable may not have been tightened properly at the factory and can work loose.
issues.next: Always put the shifter in Park as well as using the parking brake. Ask a dealer for recall 05V069000.

issues.t: Driver seat riser can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing you can feel. In a crash the driver's seat could come loose.
issues.why: A crack can form in the foot of the driver's seat riser bracket, weakening how the seat is anchored.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check for recall 04V279000. They inspect the bracket and replace it with an improved part if needed.

issues.t: Dealer trailer wiring module can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or melted wiring near the trailer hitch connector, especially when towing.
issues.why: Dealer-installed trailer hitch wiring harnesses and control modules on some early Endeavors can overheat.
issues.next: If your SUV has a dealer-installed hitch, ask a dealer about recall 04V197000 and don't use the harness until it is checked.

issues.t: High-pitched whine from the drivetrain
issues.sym: A whine or squeal that rises with speed and is most noticeable above about 50 mph or under light throttle.
issues.why: Mitsubishi issued service alerts for gear whine from the transaxle and the axle assembly. Owners report worn drivetrain parts such as the transfer case or rear differential at higher mileage.
issues.next: Have a shop pinpoint where the noise comes from and check fluid levels in the transmission, transfer case and rear differential. A failing transfer case can lock the wheels, so don't put it off if the noise gets louder.

issues.t: Rear or side window glass shatters by itself
issues.sym: A loud bang and a side, rear or liftgate window suddenly breaks with no impact, sometimes while closing the liftgate.
issues.why: Owners report tempered glass on the Endeavor shattering on its own, often linked to stress in the glass or a binding window or liftgate.
issues.next: Cover the opening to keep water out and replace the glass. If a door window keeps having trouble, check the window regulator too.

issues.t: Rear power window falls into the door
issues.sym: A rear window drops into the door and won't go back up, or the motor runs but the glass doesn't move.
issues.why: The window regulator breaks. Mitsubishi also issued service alerts for door glass coming loose from the regulator.
issues.next: Tape or cover the window and have the regulator replaced. Expect to replace it once rather than repair it.

issues.t: Interior flooding from blocked body drains
issues.sym: Water pools on the floorboards after rain or car washes, and the carpet stays wet.
issues.why: Drain paths in the body clog, so water that should run out finds its way into the cabin. Owners report it separately from the A/C drain leak.
issues.next: Have the sunroof, cowl and body drains cleared and the seals checked. Dry the interior quickly to prevent mold and electrical problems.

issues.t: Clogged catalytic converter
issues.sym: Weak acceleration, the engine feels choked at higher speeds, a check engine light or a rotten-egg smell.
issues.why: A catalytic converter can break down inside and block exhaust flow. Owners report it on the 2007 at about 95,000 miles.
issues.next: Have exhaust back pressure and codes checked. Fix any misfire first, because unburned fuel is what usually ruins converters.

issues.t: Timing belt failure
issues.sym: The engine suddenly stops running and won't restart, or there is ticking or whining from the front of the engine before it fails.
issues.why: The 3.8L V6 uses a rubber timing belt that wears out with age and mileage. Owners report timing belt failures, and others replace the belt and tensioners as maintenance.
issues.next: Check your records. If the belt has not been changed at the interval in your owner's manual, have the belt, tensioner and idler replaced before it breaks.

issues.t: Failed ignition coil causes rough running
issues.sym: The engine shakes or shudders, runs rough, and the check engine light may flash.
issues.why: An ignition coil can fail and cause a misfire. An owner reported this on a 2006 at high mileage.
issues.next: Have the misfire code read and the bad coil replaced. Don't drive long with a flashing check engine light, because it can ruin the catalytic converter.

issues.t: Airbag (SRS) warning light stays on
issues.sym: The SRS airbag light stays on. Some owners report the dealer could not get the part.
issues.why: Faults in the passenger airbag system or its sensors set the light. Owners of 2004, 2007 and 2010 models report it.
issues.next: Have the SRS codes read. The airbags may not work correctly while the light is on, so get it fixed. A used or rebuilt part may be needed if Mitsubishi no longer sells it.

issues.t: Exterior door handles snap off
issues.sym: An outside door handle or rear door handle breaks off, and the door won't open from outside.
issues.why: The handles are plastic and owners report them breaking repeatedly.
issues.next: Replace the handle. Until then, the door can usually be opened from inside.

issues.t: Sunroof wind noise
issues.sym: A whistling or rushing wind noise from the sunroof, especially at highway speed.
issues.why: The sunroof seal or the glass adjustment lets air leak past at speed. Owners report it even at low mileage.
issues.next: Ask a shop to adjust the sunroof glass and check the seal. Clean and lubricate the seal as well.

issues.t: Black paint fades and peels
issues.sym: Black paint turns chalky or white, and the clear coat peels off.
issues.why: Owners report clear coat failure on the paint of early Endeavors.
issues.next: Wash and wax often to slow it down. A body shop can repaint the worst panels.

issues.t: Tire pressure warning light flashes
issues.sym: The tire pressure (TPMS) light flashes and then stays on even when the tires are properly inflated.
issues.why: A flashing TPMS light means a system fault, usually a dead sensor battery or a failed sensor.
issues.next: Check all tire pressures, then have the TPMS sensors scanned. Replace the failed sensor and have the system relearned.
